articleTitle: Advanced Clustering Approach for Mapping Regions of Paddy Productivity in Indonesia Using Intelligent K-Means
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Asia-Pacific Conference on Geoscience, Electronics and Remote Sensing Technology (AGERS)
abstract: Paddy is an important agricultural commodity in Indonesia processed into rice, it is the main food for Indonesia. However, paddy production varies in each region which influences its price. Rice production affects by season so it has volatile prices. This paper aims to map areas in Indonesia according to paddy productivity. It uses datasets from the Ministry of Agriculture containing variables of the name of areas, paddy fields (hectare), paddy productions (ton), and paddy productivity (quintallhectare) from 2010 to 2023. It implements the Intelligent K-Means (iK-Means) algorithm. It clusters areas of provinces and districts with average Silhouette scores of 0.64 and 0.42, respectively. Clustering by provinces outputs two clusters with high and low paddy productivity. Provinces that have high paddy production are Jawa Timur, Jawa Tengah, Jawa Barat, and Sulawesi Selatan. Clustering by districts also defines two clusters of high and low paddy production. The top districts that produce paddy are Indramayu, Karawang, Subang, Banyu Asin, Lamongan, Garut, Cilacap, Bone, Bojonegoro, Cianjur, Grobogan, Sukabumi, Ngawi, Tasikmalaya, and Ogan Komering Ulu Timur.

articleTitle: USASAT-NGSO-3X Filing Analysis Using ITU-BR GIBC Software For Various Orbital Shells
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Asia-Pacific Conference on Geoscience, Electronics and Remote Sensing Technology (AGERS)
abstract: Interference is a significant problem in satellite communication operations, one of which is between Non-Geostationary Orbit (non-GSO) satellites and Geostationary Orbit (GSO) ground stations. To calculate the impact of this interference, an evaluation of the EPFD (Equivalent Power Flux Density) is carried out, which describes the average power density of the signal received at the receiving station location. This study conducted an in-depth study of the level of interference by signals from the USASAT NGSO-3X satellite in various orbital shells that affect the GSO system. By using the worst-case geometry method, the EPFD calculation can provide valuable insight into the level of interference that occurs. Based on the results of the study, it was concluded that a more in-depth study of the ITU-BR GIBC software algorithm was needed regarding the analysis of EPFD values using the worst-case geometry method. GIBC simulations show inconsistencies in the EPFD values correlated with the values set in Article 22 ITU-R and S.1503-2 ITU-R, both through aggregate and separate orbit examinations, so that a review of the ITU-R S.1503-2 algorithm is needed to ensure that interference between non-GSO satellites and GSO earth stations remains under control within the specified limits.

articleTitle: Analyzing 5G Network Performance: A Case of Bangkok's Iconic Shopping Mall
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Asia-Pacific Conference on Geoscience, Electronics and Remote Sensing Technology (AGERS)
abstract: This study conducted field tests in stationary mode at a major shopping mall in Bangkok. It utilizes two 5G smartphones and service packages from two mobile network operators (MNOs), later called MNO-X and MNO-Y, to assess 5G Quality of Service (QoS) in three zones: an indoor high zone, an indoor low zone, and an outdoor pier zone. Each MNO was tested 36 times in each zone, focusing on download (DL) and upload (UL) rates, as well as latency. Results show that MNO-Y provided higher average DL rates and lower latency than MNO-X, while MNO-X provided a higher average UL rate. Significant differences in QoS parameters between zones were also analyzed using ANOVA and t-Tests, highlighting variances likely influenced by differences in in-building coverage (IBC) and distributed antenna systems (DAS). The findings suggest that indoor QoS for DL and latency generally are better than outdoor levels, whereas UL performances were stronger outdoors. Future research is recommended to investigate technical aspects of IBC and DAS in large-scale buildings, such as major shopping malls.

articleTitle: Implementation of Data Mining Using Apriori and FP-Growth Algorithms to Determine Product Bundling Strategy in Sakinah Supermarket Keputih
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Asia-Pacific Conference on Geoscience, Electronics and Remote Sensing Technology (AGERS)
abstract: The FMCG industry in Indonesia experienced a slowdown in growth in 2023 due to national inflation, which altered consumer spending patterns. Sakinah Supermarket, a leading player in the sector, also saw a revenue decline attributed to global inflation. To address this, Sakinah plans to develop a new promotional strategy based on consumer shopping behaviours. One proposed approach is using market basket analysis to create product bundling strategies. This involves analysing transaction data through Data Mining using the Apriori and FP-Growth algorithms, which efficiently identify frequent item sets and generate association rules. The dataset used in this study includes 3634 transactions and 22,413 rows of data, which are the data transactions from January 2023 until december 2023. The algorithms will be compared based on support, confidence, and lift ratio values to determine the most accurate method. The selected algorithm's results will guide product bundling recommendations for Sakinah Supermarket. Based on the percentage value of the data processing results using the apriori and FP-Growth algorithms, it is possible to decide that Sakinah Supermarket's data is better suited to the FP-Growth approach. The resulting item combinations are Sedaap Mie and Indomie Inst with a lift ratio value of 3,7; Sunlight SBN Cuci Prg and Indomie Inst with a lift ratio value of 2,5; Soklin Softgn and Indomie Inst with a lift ratio value of 2,2; Ultra Milk Uht and Indomie Inst with a lift ratio value of 1,7; and Pepsodent PG and Indomie Inst with a lift ratio value ofl,6. All combinations show a lift value greater than 1, suggesting that the resulting combination is legitimate and suitable for bundling product items at Sakinah Supermarket.

articleTitle: Seasonal and Spatial Variations of Land Surface Temperature in DKI Jakarta: A Decade Long-Landsat-Based Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Asia-Pacific Conference on Geoscience, Electronics and Remote Sensing Technology (AGERS)
abstract: This study presents an in-depth analysis of Land Surface Temperature (LST) trends in the DKI Jakarta region using Landsat satellite imagery spanning from January 2013 to December 2023. Given the rapid urbanization and expansion in Jakarta, understanding LST patterns is crucial for assessing the impacts of urban heat islands and guiding effective urban planning strategies. To achieve this, Landsat 8 and Landsat 9 data were employed, ensuring high-quality imagery by filtering out scenes with cloud cover exceeding 45%. The research methodology involved merging the Landsat 8 and Landsat 9 datasets to create a unified image collection, which was then temporally aggregated into monthly median composites. This aggregation process helps in reducing temporal noise and capturing clear seasonal variations in temperature. The radiance values from the Landsat thermal bands were converted to temperature values in Celsius using established conversion formulas. The study's results include a time series analysis of monthly average LST, highlighting significant seasonal variations, with higher temperatures observed during the dry season and lower temperatures during the rainy season. Additionally, spatial temperature distribution maps reveal temperature gradients within Jakarta, reflecting the urban heat island effect and variations based on land use and density. This analysis provides valuable insights into the thermal dynamics of Jakarta, contributing to a better understanding of the region's climate and supporting the development of strategies to mitigate the impacts of urban heat. Future research could extend the time series and integrate additional climatic and land use data for a more comprehensive analysis.

articleTitle: Fixed-time Attitude Synchronization of Non-Identical Satellites with Unknown Dynamics Using Neural Network-Based Impulsive Control
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Asia-Pacific Conference on Geoscience, Electronics and Remote Sensing Technology (AGERS)
abstract: This research focuses on a synchronization method between two non-identical satellite systems under the influence of uncertain disturbances. For ensuring the attitude synchronization in the framework of unknown dynamics, the radial basis function-based neural network is used here. The impulsive control strategy with time delay exhibits a fixed time synchronization process which makes the proposed control strategy acceptable for real-time satellite functions under strict time constraints. Additionally, the attitude surface functions are defined in a way that the system's response is rapid in the presence of both small and large errors. The system's stability is shown by Lyapunov analysis and the efficiency of the controller is confirmed by conducting numerical simulation results.

articleTitle: Application of YOLOv11 Classification for Efficient Waste Segmentation in Australia's Recycling Facilities
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Asia-Pacific Conference on Geoscience, Electronics and Remote Sensing Technology (AGERS)
abstract: This paper investigates the use of YOLOvll, an advanced deep learning model, for waste classification in Aus-tralian recycling facilities, aiming to improve sorting accuracy and reduce contamination in line with Australia's National Waste Policy. Utilizing the RealWaste dataset, which contains over 10,000 annotated images of waste materials collected at the Whyte's Gully Waste and Resource Recovery facility in Wollongong, NSW, this study demonstrates YOLOvll's superior performance across various metrics. The YOLOvll variants achieved top-l classification accuracies ranging from 82.39% to 85.95% and top-5 accuracies from 99.37% to 99.79<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>. The highest-performing model, YOLOvllm-cls, achieved a top-l accuracy of 85.95% and an inference time of 0.5545 ms, balancing classification precision with computational efficiency. These results significantly improve upon prior models used in similar tasks, showcasing YOLOvll ‘s potential to automate waste classification, reduce human error, and enhance recycling operations.

articleTitle: Sensor Classification for CO2 Detection in IoT-Enabled Indoor Air Quality Monitoring Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Asia-Pacific Conference on Geoscience, Electronics and Remote Sensing Technology (AGERS)
abstract: Indoor air quality (IAQ) is a critical factor in ensuring the health, comfort, and productivity of individuals in indoor spaces. Among various pollutants, carbon dioxide (CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) is a primary indicator of air quality in enclosed environments. Elevated CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> levels can cause discomfort, reduced cognitive function, and even health risks when concentrations exceed safe limits. The advancement of Internet of Things (IoT) technology has significantly enhanced IAQ monitoring by enabling real-time, remote data collection, analysis, and automated control of air quality. This integration relies heavily on the use of sensors that can accurately detect CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> levels, allowing for intelligent and adaptive systems. Several types of sensors are commonly used for CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> detection in IoT-enabled IAQ monitoring systems. These sensors vary in terms of detection principle, performance, accuracy, and application suitability. This paper explores the different sensor technologies within 10 key parameters and 5 detection principles for CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> detection, focusing on their trade-off in IoT-based IAQ monitoring systems.

articleTitle: Comparison of Vegetation Index Using Aerial Imagery Data for Oil Palm Tree Health Assessment
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Asia-Pacific Conference on Geoscience, Electronics and Remote Sensing Technology (AGERS)
abstract: Oil palm plantations are vital in producing palm oil, necessitating effective monitoring for understanding plant growth and health. Remote sensing methods, particularly Vegetation Indices (VI) analysis, are crucial for extensive land monitoring. This study critically assesses and compares commonly used VI methods, including NDVI, EVI, and SAVI, in oil palm plantation monitoring. By reviewing relevant literature and employing drone imagery data, NDVI, EVI, and SAVI indices were calculated and compared for a plantation block in North Sumatra. Results indicate that while all methods show normal plant conditions, there are variations in value ranges and visualization outcomes. This research found that the NDVI provides accurate results and demonstrates consistent accuracy, making it a preferred method for oil palm monitoring followed by EVI and SA VI.

articleTitle: Geophysical Investigation of Fault Connectivity: Analyzing the Cimandiri and Lembang Faults Through Gravity and Magnetic Surveys
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Asia-Pacific Conference on Geoscience, Electronics and Remote Sensing Technology (AGERS)
abstract: This research investigates the connectivity between the Cimandiri and Lembang Faults in West Java, Indonesia, two major tectonic structures with significant implications for regional seismic activity. This study aims to identify geophysical anomalies indicative of potential interactions or stress transfer between the faults by utilizing geomagnetic and gravity surveys. Detailed data analysis, including the distribution of magnetic and gravity measurement points collected in May and August 2024, provides insights into subsurface density variations and magnetic anomalies along fault lines. Historical earthquake data is further analyzed to determine correlations in seismic events along both faults, with the objective of assessing interdependence and risk potential. Preliminary findings suggest the possibility of stress transfer between the Cimandiri and Lembang Faults, highlighting the necessity of evaluating this connection to improve earthquake preparedness and risk mitigation strategies in West Java.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Classification Model for Oil Palm Tree Health Assessment
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Asia-Pacific Conference on Geoscience, Electronics and Remote Sensing Technology (AGERS)
abstract: The oil palm tree is a highly valued plant. It is a tropical palm tree known as Elaeis guineensis. It is valued for its fruit which produces two varieties of oil: palm oil and palm kernel oil. This study explored the application of satellite and Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) imagery in assessing vegetation health through the calculation of the Visible Atmospherically Resistant Index (VARI) and Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI). Utilizing the capabilities of ArcGIS software, the imagery data are processed to generate VARI and NDVI raster layers, providing insights into oil palm tree health conditions. The workflow involves data collection, preprocessing, VARI and NDVI calculations, analysis, and visualization. The grayscale VARI and NDVI images reveal spatial patterns of vegetation health. This result contributes to land management, environmental monitoring, and agricultural decision-making processes. This study demonstrates the comparison of VARI and NDVI in terms of accuracy for oil palm tree health assessment. A new novelty from this study is that VARI has higher accuracy than NDVI.

articleTitle: Oil Spill Detection in Gulf of Thailand using Normalized Difference Index with Local Mean Reflectance
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Asia-Pacific Conference on Geoscience, Electronics and Remote Sensing Technology (AGERS)
abstract: The Gulf of Thailand is a region rich in activities. Oil drilling and transportation are an important one that plays a crucial role in the ASIAN economy. However, oil spills pose serious environmental risks and can impact human health both directly and indirectly. To improve disaster planning and management for oil spills, effective detection, monitoring, and mapping of spill areas are essential. However, detecting oil spills is a challenging task influenced by various factors, including weather conditions, observation angles, oil types, water depth and etc. Moreover, the interaction between spilled oil and different wavelengths of the electromagnetic spectrum varies, with some wavelengths performing effectively in specific conditions while failing in others. To address these challenges, this research integrates data across all wavelength ranges to enhance the accuracy and reliability of oil spill detection. This paper proposes an oil spill detection method based on the Normalized Difference Ratio. The method employs the local mean reflectance of each spectral band to calculate an individual Normalized Difference Index (NDI) relative to its surroundings. The NDIs from all bands are then combined to capture comprehensive oil spill information across the spectral range. The proposed method was evaluated using data from two sites in the Gulf of Thailand and compared with existing techniques. Both visual and quantitative results demonstrate that the method outperforms traditional approaches in detecting and mapping oil spills. This advancement offers a valuable tool for improving oil spill response and management, helping to mitigate environmental and economic damages in sensitive marine ecosystems.

articleTitle: Monitoring of Shoreline Based on Modified Normalized Difference Water Index (MNDWI) Algorithm in North Coast of Bekasi, West Java, Indonesia
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Asia-Pacific Conference on Geoscience, Electronics and Remote Sensing Technology (AGERS)
abstract: The objective is to determine shoreline changes in the coastal areas of the north coast of Bekasi, West Java, Indonesia using the Modified Normalized Difference Water Index (MNDWI) technique on Landsat Satellite Imagery. The shoreline derived from water index is obtained using Landsat time series from Google Earth Engine (GEE) includes Landsat 5 TM (1985, 1990, and 1995), Landsat 7 ETM+ (2000, 2005, and 2010), and Landsat OLI/TIRS (2015, 2020, and 2023). The water index utilizes surface reflectance instead of top-of-atmosphere reflectance obtained from the blue and shortwave infrared (SWIR 2) Landsat bands. The results show shoreline changes in the coastal area of the north coast of Bekasi, West Java, Indonesia due to abrasion and erosion at certain sites along throughout time.

articleTitle: Comparing Swiggy and Zomato: Insights from Google Play Store Reviews
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Asia-Pacific Conference on Geoscience, Electronics and Remote Sensing Technology (AGERS)
abstract: The food conveyance industry has become a fundamental piece of the current way of life, with an ever-increasing number of purchasers depending on portable applications to get to various cooking styles effectively. Given the developing dependence on these administrations, it is critical to comprehend client encounters on giant stages like Swiggy and Zomato. Breaking down client surveys of these stages not only gives bits of knowledge into the presentation of every stage but additionally impacts the more extensive elements of the food conveyance industry in India. This exploration report presents an organized dataset of surveys of Swiggy and Zomato portable applications on the Google Play Store. The main goal is to provide a precise, close examination and enable partners to identify the strengths and weaknesses of each phase. It allows a thorough customer feedback analysis to identify areas for Zomato improvement and gauge customer satisfaction with Swiggy. Opinion research is used to measure how clients feel overall about the two phases. Pessimistic client experiences may result from specific challenges that the conveyance stages confront, such as application misfires, server personal delays, or installation handling troubles. Users' expectations for seamless, efficient, personalized services are rising as they become more discerning. So, meeting or exceeding these expectations is a continuous challenge for food delivery platforms. The idea behind conducting this research is that the food delivery sector is witnessing increased competition from other food delivery platforms and new entrants and aggregators. Users may have more choices, affecting their expectations and preferences.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Noise Reduction Techniques for Body Fluid Image Enhancement
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Asia-Pacific Conference on Geoscience, Electronics and Remote Sensing Technology (AGERS)
abstract: Cancer remains a leading cause of global morbidity and mortality, with late detection significantly reducing the effectiveness of treatment options. Early diagnosis is crucial for improving survival rates, enhancing therapeutic outcomes, and reducing healthcare costs. Among various diagnostic approaches, the analysis of biomarkers in body fluids has gained prominence due to its minimally invasive nature and cost-effectiveness. However, microscopic images of body fluids often suffer from noise and poor quality, hindering accurate diagnosis. This paper investigates the effectiveness of various image filtering techniques, such as Average, Wiener, and Gaussian filters, to body fluid images degraded by Salt and Pepper and Gaussian noise at four levels. By comparing these methods, we aim to identify the most effective filter for denoising and enhancing cell images, thereby supporting the development of more accurate cancer detection systems.

articleTitle: Parallelizing Cipher Processes with Finite State Machine in MATLAB for Substitution and Transposition
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Asia-Pacific Conference on Geoscience, Electronics and Remote Sensing Technology (AGERS)
abstract: This article introduces a novel methodology for enhancing the efficiency of cipher processes by employing Finite State Machines (FSMs) within the MATLAB environment. The primary focus of this research is to improve the speed of algorithms used for both substitution and transposition ciphers, which are essential components of cryptographic practices. Recognizing the critical importance of speed in cryptographic operations, this research emphasizes the optimization of these algorithms as a key objective. Traditional encryption methods often struggle with performance limitations; thus, this paper proposes a solution by integrating parallelism into both the encryption and decryption stages through FSMs. This strategy capitalizes on the computational capabilities of modern multi-core processors, allowing for more efficient execution of cryptographic tasks. The research delineates two main phases of the proposed methodology. The first phase centers on transposition ciphers, while the second phase focuses on substitution ciphers. Data encryption is carried out via a meticulously defined FSM-based procedure that alters the input data by substituting and transposing values in accordance with a specified cryptographic key. The concurrent execution of both phases results in a substantial decrease in processing time. Empirical findings indicate that the processing duration is under 1 second for data sizes ranging from 8 to 129 bits, while encrypting and decrypting 1 billion bits of data takes approximately 162 seconds. The improvements in processing speed and the adaptability of these methods highlight their potential as effective solutions for secure data processing applications, which encompass secure communication and the advancement of sophisticated cryptographic protocols.

articleTitle: Analyzing the Impact of Mandalika Special Economic Zone (SEZ) Development on Land Surface Temperature (LST) Using Landsat 8 Satellite Imagery
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Asia-Pacific Conference on Geoscience, Electronics and Remote Sensing Technology (AGERS)
abstract: This study examines the impact of urban devel-opment, particularly the Mandalika Special Economic Zone (SEZ) and Mandalika Circuit, on the Land Surface Tem-perature (LST) and vegetation dynamics in Kuta Village, Central Lombok, Indonesia. Utilizing Landsat 8 satellite imagery from 2014 to 2023, the study evaluates temporal changes in LST and the Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) to understand the effects of rapid urbanization on the local environment. LST and NDVI values were derived from surface reflectance and thermal infrared bands, with annual averages computed for each year to observe trends over time. Spatial analysis revealed signifi-cant increases in LST, particularly in the southeastern re-gion of Kuta Village, where urbanization and infrastructure expansion have led to the formation of an urban heat island effect. In contrast, vegetation health, measured by NDVI, showed a decrease in areas affected by construction and land use changes, yet the overall NDVI values across the village remained relatively stable. The study employed the Mann-Kendall test to assess trends, finding that while there were notable localized changes in both LST and NDVI, the broader long-term trends across the region did not exhibit statistically significant shifts. These findings underscore the localized impact of urban development, highlighting areas where temperature increases and vegetation loss are most prominent. The results emphasize the importance of sus-tainable urban planning strategies to mitigate the adverse effects of urbanization, such as increasing green spaces and adopting environmentally friendly construction practices. Sustainable urban management practices are crucial to balance development needs with environmental sustainabil-ity, ensuring long-term ecological and social resilience in the region.

articleTitle: Estimating Above Ground Forest Biomass Using High-Resolution NAIP Imagery, Machine Learning, and Google Earth Engine
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Asia-Pacific Conference on Geoscience, Electronics and Remote Sensing Technology (AGERS)
abstract: Accurate Forest Aboveground Biomass (AGB) mapping is essential for understanding carbon storage in ecosystems, global carbon cycles, and effective forest management. Remote sensing (RS) technologies and advanced machine learning algorithms (MLAs) provide a reliable way to estimate AGB. This study explores using National Agriculture Imagery Program (NAIP) data, field measurements, and topographic variables for estimating AGB in Drew County, Arkansas, USA. The study used features derived from NAIP imagery, such as vegetation indices and texture metrics, as well as data from digital elevation models (DEMs) as input variables for three ML algorithms: Random Forest (RF), Gradient Tree Boosting (GTB), and Classification and Regression Trees (CART), tested across 15 different combinations of feature variables. Of the models tested, RF performed best, achieving the highest prediction accuracy <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathrm{R}^{2}=0.77, \text{RMSE}=34.85 \ \mathrm{t}/\text{ha})$</tex>, outperforming GTB and CART. The use of multiple feature variables significantly improved the accuracy of predictions in all the algorithms, with the most significant contributions to model performance coming from vegetation indices and texture metrics derived from NAIP imagery. In contrast, relying only on elevation-based variables resulted in lower accuracy, underscoring the importance of using various data sources. The study also found that AGB was overestimated in non-forested areas when only topographic variables were used, highlighting the need for a balanced integration of features. This research provides a scalable and reproducible framework for continuous AGB monitoring at high spatial resolutions, utilizing the strengths of ML and advanced RS data.
