articleTitle: Integration of PS-InSAR and SBAS Methods With Different DEM for Monitoring the Activity of the Kendeng Fault in the Surabaya and Waru Segments
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Asia-Pacific Conference on Geoscience, Electronics and Remote Sensing Technology (AGERS)
abstract: The Kendeng Fault system, a prominent geological feature in East Java, significantly influences seismic activity in the region, particularly in Surabaya City. Understanding the dynamics of this fault system is crucial due to its potential impact on urban areas and infrastructure. This study focuses on monitoring fault activity in Surabaya by utilizing external Digital Elevation Model (DEM) data, specifically DEMNAS and Copernicus. We employ Sentinel-1 descending data collected from January 2022 to August 2024 to facilitate a comprehensive analysis. The research integrates two advanced remote sensing techniques: Persistent Scatterer Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (PS-InSAR) and Small Baseline Area Subset (SBAS). Both methods are adept at analyzing ground displacement, and their integration enhances the accuracy of deformation mapping. Notably, external DEM data is utilized during the processing stages of both PS-InSAR and SBAS, significantly improving the geospatial accuracy of and distribution point ground displacement to analyze and detail the results. Our findings reveal significant ground displacement patterns that are correlated with the activity of the Kendeng Fault, with a particular focus on its Waru and Surabaya segments. This research not only contributes to a deeper understanding of the seismic risks associated with the fault but also highlights the effectiveness of utilizing satellite radar data in monitoring geological hazards. Ultimately, the insights gained from this study can inform urban planning and disaster preparedness initiatives in Surabaya, aiming to enhance the resilience of the city against potential seismic events.

articleTitle: Hazard Modeling of Sulawesi-Maluku Earthquakes Using Space-Time ETAS: Comparing Long Decay and Short Decay Densities
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Asia-Pacific Conference on Geoscience, Electronics and Remote Sensing Technology (AGERS)
abstract: The space-time ETAS (Epidemic-Type Aftershock Sequence) model is a point process-based framework for earthquake modeling that leverages complete seismic catalogs to predict earthquake occurrences by capturing both spatial and temporal dependencies. It incorporates a long decay spatial density function, which models the gradual decrease in aftershock probability with increasing distance from the mainshocks. However, the Sulawesi-Maluku region, characterized by complex tectonic interactions and active subduction zones such as the Halmahera and Sangihe arcs, experiences frequent shallow earthquake swarms, exhibit a higher degree of clustering centered around the mainshocks, which may suggest an alternative of spatial density function within the space-time ETAS model. This study compares the commonly used long decay and short decay spatial density in the space-time ETAS model to fit the earthquake catalog in the Sulawesi-Maluku based on model complexity, computational time, and intensity prediction. Findings reveal that the short-decay function outperforms the long-decay counterpart, efficiently identifying high-seismicity areas in the Halmahera and Sangihe arcs, the Palu Koro-Matano fault zone, and the Seram Sea. This study advances seismic risk assessment and supports disaster mitigation efforts in Sulawesi-Maluku.

articleTitle: Development of a Remote Sensing System for Real-Time Detection of Military Threats
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Asia-Pacific Conference on Geoscience, Electronics and Remote Sensing Technology (AGERS)
abstract: To strengthen the national defense system, advances in remote sensing technology are essential, especially to detect military threats that could threaten sovereignty. These threats can be physical or non-physical, such as cyber-attacks that can damage vital infrastructure. Therefore, effective border monitoring is critical to maintaining the security and stability of the country. Although remote sensing technology is developing rapidly, several issues hinder its implementation, such as inadequate infrastructure and lack of employee training. Previous research has not fully studied how various advanced technologies can be incorporated into Indonesia's border area defense system that is responsive and operates in real time. The purpose of this study is to see how well remote sensing systems detect military threats and evaluate the problems that arise when implementing them. In addition, this study aims to provide strategic suggestions that will help improve national defense. This research utilizes a literature review of relevant articles and analyzes information to gain a further understanding of advances in remote sensing technology and its applications in defense. Studies show that technologies such as radar, CCTV, and artificial intelligence (AI) can improve threat detection in border areas. AI-based radars enable faster identification and classification of threats, and cloud-based CCTV improves real-time monitoring. The findings from this study suggest that the development and utilization of advanced remote sensing technologies can improve Indonesia's defense system. By addressing infrastructure and personnel training issues, the country can more effectively safeguard its sovereignty and stability by improving responses to military and non-military threats.

articleTitle: Analysis of Traffic Accident Risk in Nganjuk Using Point Process on a Linear Network with Lasso Regularization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Asia-Pacific Conference on Geoscience, Electronics and Remote Sensing Technology (AGERS)
abstract: The Nganjuk Region of East Java has a very high incidence of traffic accidents, largely attributable to the high traffic density. To conduct a comprehensive analysis of the risk of traffic accidents in the Nganjuk Region, in this study we employ detailed data involving the coordinate locations of traffic accidents integrated with environmental factors, road geometrical features, and remote sensing. To perform the analysis, we consider the Poisson point process model on a linear network. Furthermore, we combine the standard maximum likelihood technique with Lasso regularization to perform variable selection and parameter estimation simultaneously. We develop the algorithm by considering three techniques consecutively namely the Berman-Turner approach, Taylor expansion, and coordinate descent algorithm (CDA). Among the six covariates used in this study, we select three that are significant for the intensity of risk accidents in the N ganj uk Region: distance to the nearest traffic light location, road types, and number of lanes. This information is useful for the Nganjuk Region government as a consideration in formulating policies to prevent traffic accidents and to provide useful information to the community and the government regarding locations prone to traffic accidents.

articleTitle: Accuracy Results Comparison of Machine Learning Classification for Mangroves on Worldview-2 Satellite Imagery
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Asia-Pacific Conference on Geoscience, Electronics and Remote Sensing Technology (AGERS)
abstract: Mangrove forests are one of the highest carbon stores in tropical forests and the amount is very high compared to the average carbon storage in other types of forests in the world. High-resolution satellite imagery provides the ability to obtain finer details, allowing more accurate identification of different types of vegetation and mangrove structures. Worldview - 2 high resolution image can cover large mapping areas, making it more efficient to monitor changes on a large scale. The location of mangroves with limited access required remote sensing techniques which were relatively more cost and time efficient compared to field survey. Machine learning-based classification methods were compared to determine the most accurate and reliable performance results for mangrove classification. In this study, comparisons were made using accuracy test points to assess the level of accuracy of mangrove and another land cover classification generated from the Iso Cluster, Maximum Likelihood, Random Forest and Support Vector Machine methods. According to this study, the four machine learning displayed overall accuracy above 0.5. For kappa accuracy, only Iso Cluster Classification displayed value slightly below 0.5 (0.49). Four machine learning able to distinguish mangrove remarkably with user and producer accuracy 1.0. Worldview - 2 spatial resolution contribute to this accuracy, which enable classification to perform with 0.5 meter resolution. Random forest outperformed another machine learning classification with kappa accuracy 0.88 even without additional parameter and expected to overcome challenges in mapping mangrove vegetation which often has spectral values similar to other vegetation and located in quite heterogeneous ecosystem environment.

articleTitle: Assessing the Economic Impact of Peat Fires on Industrial Plantation Forests in Mesuji Subdistrict, South Sumatra, Indonesia
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Asia-Pacific Conference on Geoscience, Electronics and Remote Sensing Technology (AGERS)
abstract: South Sumatra is home to extensive peatlands, with a significant portion situated in Ogan Komering Ilir Regency. Among these areas, the Mesuji subdistrict stands out as a critical region, hosting Industrial Plantation Forests (IPFs) primarily planted with Acacia mangium, a vital economic resource. This study assesses the economic losses caused by peat fires in Mesuji, which have persisted since 2015, disrupting livelihoods and degrading ecological functions. Using secondary data and valuation techniques, the study quantifies the economic value of key ecosystem services, including timber production, honey production, and water cycle and hydrological regulation. The results indicate a total estimated loss of approximately forty-two trillion rupiahs, with timber production accounting for the majority of these losses. These findings emphasize the urgency of implementing effective peatland restoration and fire prevention strategies. Moreover, the study offers a framework to better understand the socioeconomic and ecological consequences of IPF losses, providing valuable insights for policy development and public engagement.

articleTitle: Oceanographic Aspects in Marine Cadastre
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Asia-Pacific Conference on Geoscience, Electronics and Remote Sensing Technology (AGERS)
abstract: Oceanographic aspects play a crucial role in compiling an effective marine cadastre. This research examines how oceanographic data is utilized to map the potential and constraints of marine space utilization. An in-depth analysis reveals that integrating oceanographic data into marine cadastres enhances accuracy in spatial planning, disaster mitigation, and the sustainable management of marine resources. In the context of Jakarta Coastal Bay (Teluk Jakarta), which features numerous small islands, 13 river estuaries, and a coastline utilized for marine tourism, military activities, fishing ports, passenger terminals, and navigation routes, the role of marine cadastre is particularly vital. This framework supports the management of various activities, including fishing and aquaculture, ensuring a balanced and sustainable approach to resource use. However, challenges persist, including limited data availability, the complexity of oceanographic processes, and insufficient institutional capacity. Despite these hurdles, the potential benefits of integration are significant. Sediment transport, a dynamic process influenced by various oceanographic parameters, plays a vital role in shaping beach morphology, seabed structure, and coastal ecosystems. Key oceanographic parameters affecting sediment transport include waves, currents, tides, sediment characteristics, and bathymetry. This ongoing process continuously alters the morphology of the seabed and has substantial implications for marine space management, particularly along coastlines. This research analyses the role of sediment transport as an essential oceanographic aspect in developing a Marine Cadastral Model, focusing on the changes over time caused by sediment transport dynamics. By understanding these interactions, effective management strategies can be formulated to address the challenges faced in marine spatial planning.

articleTitle: Gaussian Splatting for Rapid and Precise 3D Modeling in Mapping Application: Literature Review
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Asia-Pacific Conference on Geoscience, Electronics and Remote Sensing Technology (AGERS)
abstract: Creating 3D models quickly and accurately is a persistent challenge in mapping applications, where balancing computational efficiency and precision is essential. Close-range photogrammetry, a widely used technique, generates dense point clouds from overlapping images, forming the foundation for detailed 3D models. Traditionally, Mesh Based reconstruction has been employed to transform these point clouds into continuous surfaces, enabling high-detail visualizations. However, Mesh Based methods are computationally intensive and time-consuming, limiting their feasibility for real-time or large-scale applications. Neural Radiance Fields (NeRF) offer an alternative with photo-realistic outputs but are resource-heavy and less practical for large datasets. Similarly, Voxel Based methods provide structured data representation but often struggle with fine detail and scalability. Gaussian Splatting, a recent breakthrough, offers a transformative approach to addressing these challenges. By using continuous Gaussian functions, it rapidly processes dense point clouds without the need for computationally expensive mesh generation, enabling efficient and precise 3D modeling. This review explores how Gaussian Splatting compares with traditional Mesh Based reconstruction, NeRF, and voxel techniques in terms of speed, scalability, and accuracy. It highlights its advantages in applications such as urban mapping, industrial inspections, and geospatial analysis, particularly in scenarios demanding rapid turnarounds and real-time performance. The discussion also examines the interplay between these methods, emphasizing how Gaussian Splatting overcomes limitations in close-range photogrammetry workflows. By analyzing advancements, challenges, and practical use cases, this paper establishes Gaussian Splatting as a cutting-edge solution for rapid and precise 3D modeling in modern mapping applications.

articleTitle: Numerical Simulation of Seawall and Mangrove Effectiveness as Tsunami Barriers for Yogyakarta International Airport
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Asia-Pacific Conference on Geoscience, Electronics and Remote Sensing Technology (AGERS)
abstract: Yogyakarta International Airport (YIA) is located on the southern coast of Java Island which potentially vulnerable to tsunami disaster. Based on data from BNPB (N ational Agency for Disaster Countermeasure), the southern coast of Java is a high priority area with a high tsunami risk. YIA has the potential to be hit by a tsunami triggered by an Mw 8.8 earthquake source. Ensuring comprehensive measures is essensial to maintain airport infrastructure and protect lives in the event of a disaster. This study conducted various tsunami mitigation using a numerical model by simulating eight different conditions. The results show that integrating natural barriers, such as mangroves, with seawalls enhances mitigation performance. The combination of mangroves and as-meter seawall provides protection similar to that of a standalone 10-meter seawall, while the combination of mangroves and a 10-meter seawall achieves results comparable to a 1S-meter seawall. The most effective scenario is the combination of mangroves and a 1S-meter seawall, which provides full protection to the airport and reduces inundation in nearby areas.

articleTitle: Prediction of Earthquake Intensity and Location in Sumatra Using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Asia-Pacific Conference on Geoscience, Electronics and Remote Sensing Technology (AGERS)
abstract: Earthquake prediction is important to help mitigate the risks and damage associated with seismic events, leading to potentially saving lives and reducing economic losses. To predict earthquake events, the Epidemic-Type Aftershock Sequences (ETAS) model is often employed, which analyzes detailed earthquake catalog data by considering a statistical model incorporating seismological laws. However, the ETAS model often fails to predict earthquakes' future occurrences. To overcome this issue, we combine the ETAS model with deep learning methods to enhance prediction performance. We integrate the ETAS model with Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) and Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) architectures. By optimizing zone divisions and time-step configurations in the Sumatra region, our implementation demonstrates that this technique significantly improves the accuracy of prediction of earthquake intensity and location, marking substantial progress in seismic research and disaster prevention strategies.

articleTitle: Analysis of Building Segmentation Method for Calculating Photovoltaic Potential Area Using Segment Anything Model (SAM) on the Massachusetts Building Dataset
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Asia-Pacific Conference on Geoscience, Electronics and Remote Sensing Technology (AGERS)
abstract: Accurate roof segmentation in aerial images is essential for precise calculation of photovoltaic potential, which is increasingly important for optimizing solar energy utilization. This study aims to enhance roof segmentation precision by developing an architecture based on the Segment Anything Model (SAM) and comparing its performance to a baseline UNET architecture. We evaluated the inherent differences between instance segmentation (SAM) and semantic segmentation (UNET) approaches. The predicted roof areas of the proposed SAM-based instance segmentation model were quite accurate, hence masking those areas was facilitated. Some of the performance metrics include accuracy, Dice coefficient, and IoU. With the SAM model, an accuracy of 85.48%, a Dice coefficient of 57%, an IoU of 40.4%, while UNET established an accuracy of 84.89%, a Dice coefficient of 84.7<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>, and an IoU of 73.6% accordingly. In fact, these results really show that while the SAM model is more accurate, the UNET model outperforms it in terms of Dice coefficient and IoU, probably because of fundamental differences between instance and semantic segmentation approaches. As conclusion, instance segmentation models such as SAM have shown their great potential in detecting roofs, whereas semantic segmentation models like UNET perform better in detecting them. A web application was developed using Streamlit and FastAPI to visualize segmentation results, effectively mapping building roofs but with room for improvement.

articleTitle: Enhanced Approach to Predict Early Stage Chronic Kidney Disease
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Asia-Pacific Conference on Geoscience, Electronics and Remote Sensing Technology (AGERS)
abstract: The prevalence of early kidney disease (EKD) is a major public health issue that affects the well-being of patients. In order to effectively manage this illness, an early diagnosis is crucial. Here, we introduce a deep incremental learning(DIL) model that can reliably foretell when this disease would manifest in its early phases. We are testing three models: Deep Belief Network (DBN), Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU), and a new approach known as CNN+DBN. Both with and without hyperparameter adjustment are considered in this study's comparison of three models. The model achieved a 98.1% accuracy rate after training with hyperparameter tuning on a dataset of chronic renal disease. In its early stages, it shows promise as a treatment for this illness. The DBN model better handles all metrics used to evaluate model performance-accuracy, recall, F1 score, area under the curve (AUC), and precision. This research introduces a convolutional neural network (CNN) model that integrates the DBN's DIL capabilities with the CNN's feature extraction capabilities. It is capable of effectively capturing data with geographical dependencies. The model is able to process and forecast the early stages of kidney disease by utilizing the retrieved features. Combining the CNN and DBN techniques improved the accuracy of the model. It outperforms GRU+DBN models and achieves 97.15 percent accuracy with the help of hyperparameter optimization. We then proceed to process this data using the CNN+DBN model. The combined model with hyperparameter adjustment outperformed the GRU+DBN models with an accuracy of 97.15 percent. Hyperparameter adjustment also enhances the model's performance. Here lies the robustness of the applied model.

articleTitle: Blockchain-Based Tokenization for Green Bonds: A Model for Transparency and Compliance in Sustainable Finance
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Asia-Pacific Conference on Geoscience, Electronics and Remote Sensing Technology (AGERS)
abstract: Green bonds, financial instruments designed to fund environmentally sustainable projects, are pivotal in achieving global sustainability goals. However, their adoption faces significant challenges, including limited and inconsistent impact reporting, fragmented regulatory frameworks, and restricted market accessibility for smaller investors. Tokenization, the process of converting real-world assets into digital tokens, offers a transformative solution by leveraging blockchain to improve traceability, automate compliance, and democratize access. This paper proposes a blockchain-based tokenization framework leveraging Ethereum's robust, scalable, and widely adopted ecosystem, providing transparency and smart contract capabilities essential for green bond management. The framework integrates fractional ownership via ERC-20 tokens, directly addressing the issue of limited market accessibility by enabling broader participation from smaller investors. By resolving these operational bottlenecks, the proposed model enhances trust among stakeholders, fosters inclusivity in green finance, and supports global sustainability goals, particularly advancing SDG 13 (Climate Action) and SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure).

articleTitle: Literature Review: Development of a Local Mean Sea Surface (MSS) Model for Shallow Waters Using Satellite Altimetry Data and in situ Measurements
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Asia-Pacific Conference on Geoscience, Electronics and Remote Sensing Technology (AGERS)
abstract: Sea Surface Height (SSH), Sea Level Anomalies (SLA), and Mean Sea Surface (MSS) are essential parameters for comprehending sea levels, particularly in the tropical waters of Indonesia. Global MSS models frequently fall short in capturing the local dynamics influenced by phenomena such as ENSO and thunderstorms. A review of 10 studies revealed significant gaps, including the lack of tropical-specific geophysical corrections, limited utilization of high-resolution multi-sensor data, and an absence of local hydrodynamic models. To address these shortcomings, future research should prioritize the development of tropical-specific corrections, the integration of multi-sensor data, and the application of dynamic models to improve MSS accuracy and enhance the understanding of seasonal variability.

articleTitle: Designing IT Governance Framework with Consideration of UU PDP Compliance: A Strategic Approach for Data Protection and Management
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Asia-Pacific Conference on Geoscience, Electronics and Remote Sensing Technology (AGERS)
abstract: Achieving alignment between business operations, Information Technology (IT) and regulatory compliance is a top priority for most organizations, including in the healthcare business sector. Hospitals as organizations, aside from running IT processes to support services to patients, also have to maintain a level of compliance with IT regulations. To ensure reliable IT management, comply with regulations and remain aligned with hospital business goals and strategies, it is necessary to develop an enterprise governance of IT that is reliable, supports business processes and is responsive to any amendments or additions to applicable IT regulations. The goal of this study is to develop efficient corporate governance in the healthcare industry by utilizing the COBIT 2019 framework. Qualitative and quantitative methods were used to identify key governance and management objectives. By engaging in various activities with hospital management, we reached conclusions about the governance design and suggested several governance and management objectives that can support the main business processes while still paying attention to the level of compliance with regulations that must be met. Hopefully, these recommendations can serve as guidance for similar organizations in terms of implementing an IT governance system using COBIT 2019.

articleTitle: Bibliometric Analysis of Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) Remote Sensing Satellite Data Utilization for Rice Paddy Mapping
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Asia-Pacific Conference on Geoscience, Electronics and Remote Sensing Technology (AGERS)
abstract: This study conducts a comprehensive bibliometric analysis to evaluate the application of Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) remote sensing data in rice paddy mapping. SAR technology offer solutions for mapping rice paddy, especially in areas with frequent cloud cover. This analysis draws from 168 relevant articles published between 1997 and 2024, sourced from the Web of Science (WoS) database. Various bibliometric methods were applied, including co-citation, co-authorship, and keyword analysis. The research highlights leading authors, journals, and institutions, while also focusing on collaborations at country and institutional levels. The results revealed the increase of publication started in 2017 as there is a lot of open-access SAR data availability. The three countries with the largest number of publications were the China (47.0%), the United States (19.0%), and India (12.5%). Based on the number of publications, Chinese Academy Science was the institution with the most publications. This study showed that Sentinel-1 data and C-band SAR data were the most used data for mapping rice paddy. Keyword co-occurrence analysis revealed emerging trends such as the integration of SAR data and other remote sensing sensor as well as machine learning algorithm utilization such as Support Vector Machine (SVM), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM), Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU), and Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) to handle big data remote sensing analysis. This study contributes to the field by offering a holistic understanding of SAR applications in agriculture, providing valuable insights for researchers, policymakers, and practitioners aiming to address challenges in rice production.

articleTitle: Rethinking Soil Diagnostics: Why IoT-Based Soil Sensors are Essential for the Future of Precision Agriculture
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Asia-Pacific Conference on Geoscience, Electronics and Remote Sensing Technology (AGERS)
abstract: The agricultural sector is under pressure to increase productivity to sustainably meet the global demand for food. Precision agriculture, depending on real-time data from the soil, offers an opportunity to optimize resource use and enhance crop yields. Disposable test kits, MOET, chemical analysis, and XRF traditional testing methods for soils are inefficient in terms of cost, environmental impact, and scalability. This review has brought out some of the benefits that can be accrued when soil diagnostics rely on the loT technologies, which will include real-time monitoring, high accuracy, and sustainability. The paper further talks about future research directions in topics involving AI integration and energy-efficient systems for loT.

articleTitle: Rapid Assessment of Economic Impacts from Inundation in Karawang, Indonesia: A Multi-Platform Geospatial Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Asia-Pacific Conference on Geoscience, Electronics and Remote Sensing Technology (AGERS)
abstract: Inundation poses significant challenges to the economic stability of Karawang, Indonesia, a key rice production region located near the coastline and at low elevations. These areas are highly vulnerable to flooding from high rainfall and sea level rise events. Remote sensing data plays a critical role in monitoring these events. This study combines several geospatial tools—SatGPT, Google Earth Engine (GEE), QGIS, and WebGIS—to conduct a rapid assessment of inundation impacts and associated economic losses over the past 13 years (2007-2020). The analysis found that approximately 30,790 hectares were inundated, with croplands experiencing the most severe damage. The estimated total economic losses amounted to USD 177,215,000, affecting croplands, forests, wetlands, built-up areas, and mangroves. The results were validated against data from Indonesia's National Disaster Management Authority (BNPB), ensuring high accuracy. This study introduces two key novelties: the first use of SatGPT in an Indonesian context and the innovative integration of SatGPT, GEE, QGIS, and WebGIS for a rapid assessment of inundation impacts and economic losses. These findings highlight the potential of geospatial platforms for quick disaster impact assessment and provide valuable insights for improving disaster risk management strategies in Indonesia.

articleTitle: Smart Algae Cultivation: IoT-Driven Incubators and Solar Energy for Sustainable Growth in Oman
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Asia-Pacific Conference on Geoscience, Electronics and Remote Sensing Technology (AGERS)
abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) plays a crucial role in simplifying life by connecting devices and systems to monitor and control various aspects of daily activities. In Oman, IoT has been integrated across multiple sectors to build a digitally advanced and sustainable nation, aligning with the country's vision of becoming a leader in smart technologies. This project, developed by a team of electronics and communications engineering, focuses on the innovative use of algae-a natural resource that is abundantly available in Oman. Algae can be harnessed for various applications, including food production, cosmetics, pharmaceuticals, and biofuels, offering a sustainable alternative to traditional resources. However, algae growth requires precise environmental conditions, including optimal temperature, humidity, light intensity, and nutrient levels. To address these challenges, the project proposes the use of IoT-enabled incubators, which can continuously monitor and regulate these parameters in realtime. By integrating sensors and smart control systems, the IoT incubators will ensure that algae are cultivated under ideal conditions, enhancing productivity and efficiency. Furthermore, the project will incorporate renewable energy sources, particularly solar power, to operate the system sustainably. This not only aligns with Oman's renewable energy goals but also reduces the ecological footprint of algae cultivation. Through this project, we aim to contribute to the diversification of Oman's economy by promoting sustainable practices and encouraging innovation in the use of natural resources. The proposed system exemplifies how IoT and renewable energy can combine to create a greener, more efficient future.

articleTitle: The Importance of Cloud Monitoring Services with A Comprehensive Review of Essential Tools
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Asia-Pacific Conference on Geoscience, Electronics and Remote Sensing Technology (AGERS)
abstract: Cloud computing is increasingly becoming de-facto-enabling technologies and advances on both the hardware and software fronts, further compounding their business value delivered to users, increasing the management complexity for cloud administrators in order to provide end-to-end service availability. One set of these tools is cloud server monitoring and network tools for system administrators. Previous studies have addressed different topics on cloud computing such as the properties and technologies related to it, as well as privacy and security issues, but cloud monitoring tools have not been systematically studied so far. This looks at what you really need to be able to do with Cloud Monitoring and what you may want to do, available from open source, Commercial or Enterprise level providers. High Impact, Proper monitoring enables adaptation of the scaling of resources based on the load, detecting service problems and tracking usage patterns in different end users, in turn helping improve cloud computing. In this paper we will conduct a review of essential tools in cloud monitoring services explaining their use as was mentioned in the recent literature highlighting the importance and the usability in terms of efficiency and security.

articleTitle: Spatial Analysis of the Relationship of the Borneo Vortex Phenomenon to Rain in West Borneo
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Asia-Pacific Conference on Geoscience, Electronics and Remote Sensing Technology (AGERS)
abstract: In November, December, January, and February throughout the year there is a phenomenon of the Borneo Vortex in the Northwest of Kalimantan Island to the southern part of the South China Sea. This phenomenon is formed continuously and is often associated with heavy rains and floods. Several previous studies have stated that there is an influence of the Borneo Vortex on atmospheric dynamics and changes in the amount of rainfall in certain regions. This study identifies and maps the relationship of the Borneo Vortex to rainfall to determine the influence of the Borneo Vortex in each region of West Kalimantan. The results showed that the highest frequency of the Borneo Vortex occurred in December at 32.6%. The relationship of the Borneo Vortex event to rain is determined by the value of the determination coefficient which is then tested F to select a significant value. IDW interpolation with power values of 1 to 4 was used to spatially analyze the relationship between the Borneo Vortex and rain in West Kalimantan. The results showed that the influence of the Borneo Vortex event on rainy days was more evenly distributed for the West Kalimantan region with medium criteria as many as 127 sub-districts or 75.6%, while the effect on rainfall with low, medium, and high threshold criteria was 60%, 35.4%, and 4.6%, respectively. The high criteria are more dominant in the northern and southern regions of West Kalimantan.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Models for Tsunami Forecasting
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Asia-Pacific Conference on Geoscience, Electronics and Remote Sensing Technology (AGERS)
abstract: Tsunami induced by seismic earthquake has generated significant disasters in the big cities around coastal regions. One of the most disastrous tsunami events, the 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami has killed 230.000 human casualties and destructed enormous infrastructures and economy in the coastal areas of several countries in the East and South Asia. The negative impacts of tsunami have initiated the vital need for an accurate and fast tsunami early warning system to anticipate infrastructure destruction and human casualties. This paper focuses on the development of a hybrid tsunami forecasting model by utilizing Delft3D-FLOW numerical models and data-driven models using computational intelligence to simulate and forecast tsunami wave amplitudes. Several deep machine learning models were built properly and optimized using Convolutional Neural Network and Long Short- Term Memory algorithms with single and multi-steps prediction methods. The proposed tsunami models provide reliable tsunami forecasts to be utilized for a real-time tsunami early warning system.

articleTitle: Parameter Estimation and Application of Spatial Extreme Value Modeling with Peaks over Threshold - Kumaraswamy Generalized Pareto (POT-KumGP) Method (Case Study: Extreme Rainfall in Maluku province)
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Asia-Pacific Conference on Geoscience, Electronics and Remote Sensing Technology (AGERS)
abstract: Extreme weather events are one of the phenomena that cause unavoidable losses in various sectors and have a serious impact on aspects of life. These impacts can be minimized by studying the patterns and characteristics of extreme events. Extreme Value Theory (EVT) is one of the statistical techniques to detect extreme events. In order to detect extreme events in many locations (multivariate), this technique was then developed into spatial extreme value (SEV). This research applies the Peaks Over-Threshold method to excessive rainfall situations using an extreme value model based on the Kumaraswamy Generalized-Pareto Distribution. This model is performed by combining the generalized Pareto and Kumaraswamy distributions. In this study, the POT-KumGP model will be applied to monthly rainfall data from 1990–2023 in Maluku Province. Extreme values are determined based on threshold selection with visualization of the mean residual life plot. A distribution suitability test using Kolmogorov-Smirnov test statistics and a probability plot is performed to validate whether the model fits the Kum-GP distribution. If the model is suitable, parameter estimation will be carried out using maximum likelihood estimation (MLE) and continued with BFGS numerical iteration. Then a trend surface model will be formed to connect longitude and latitude variables with parameter estimates so as to further increase the robustness of the analysis. The best model is selected based on the smallest AIC value and used to calculated the return level for the next few periods. This research aims to build a POT-KumGP spatial extreme value model and get the return level estimation results for the next few periods in Maluku Province in order to inform future disaster management policies or strategies.

articleTitle: Exploring Volcanic Activity Through Open Data in Mount Ruang's 2024 Eruption
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Asia-Pacific Conference on Geoscience, Electronics and Remote Sensing Technology (AGERS)
abstract: Mount Ruang underwent a significant eruption between April and May 2024, prompting the Center for Volcanology and Geological Hazard Mitigation (PVMBG) to issue hazard warnings and elevate the alert level based on data from volcanic observation posts. This study examines the eruption dynamics using data from Sentinel-1 (radar sensors) and Sentinel-2 (optical sensors) satellites. Enabled by the Copernicus Program, which facilitates Earth observation through the Sentinel satellite series, the study leverages cloud-based, on-demand data processing to analyze surface deformation and land cover changes. Time-series Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (InSAR) techniques, applied to Sentinel-1 SAR data processed via HyP3, were used to monitor surface deformation before and after the eruption. Additionally, Sentinel-2 imagery was employed to assess land cover changes. The results reveal ground inflation and deflation of approximately 15 cm preceding and following the eruption, respectively. Furthermore, vegetated land cover was reduced by approximately 866 hectares due to volcanic materials. This study demonstrates the value of freely available satellite data and open-source processing tools for understanding volcanic activity and its environmental impacts.

articleTitle: Deep Learning and CNN-Based Approach for Efficient Detection of Potato Leaf Diseases
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Asia-Pacific Conference on Geoscience, Electronics and Remote Sensing Technology (AGERS)
abstract: Potato is a maj or food crop worldwide, providing essential nutrients to millions. However, various diseases can severely affect potato crops, leading to reduced yield and quality. Early disease detection is crucial for effective disease management and control. This study presents a deep learning-based approach using CNN to autonomously diagnose potato leaf diseases. The model leverages the Plant Village dataset, which contains images of potato leaves in both healthy and diseased states. The proposed method demonstrates high accuracy in identifying multiple potato leaf diseases, offering promising results for application in precision agriculture. By utilizing CNN s, the model effectively detects and classifies disease symptoms, providing a reliable tool for early intervention in agricultural practices. The approach's potential impact on improving crop yield and minimizing losses due to diseases is highlighted, making it a significant contribution to smart farming techniques. The study underscores the importance of deep learning in modern agricultural practices and its role in enhancing disease management strategies.

articleTitle: Co-channel Interference in GSO High Throughput Multi-beam Satellite in Indonesia: Study Link Budget and Capacity Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Asia-Pacific Conference on Geoscience, Electronics and Remote Sensing Technology (AGERS)
abstract: Current satellite technology has developed rapidly from traditional satellites to High Throughput Satellite (HTS) because it offers the advantages of multibeam antennas and reuse frequencies. Nevertheless, intersystem interference exists. This study discusses Co-Channel Interference (CCI) in the 4-reuse color scheme on an 8-beam GSO HTS with Ku-band frequencies in Indonesia. The analysis was conducted by analyzing the link budget and capacity before and after interference on the user communication side, forward downlink, and return uplink. The results of the link budget before CCI, Carrier to Noise ratio or C/N on Beam 1 to 8 ranging from 23.34 dB to 23.50 dB. And C/N on the return uplink is 18.74 dB to 19.07 dB. Then after interference, the Carrier to Noise plus Interference Ratio or C/(N+I) on the forward downlink produces 11.96 dB to 12.15 dB. While the return uplink produces C/(N+I) of 13.91 to 14.05 dB for Beam 1 to Beam 8. Because CCI decreases signal quality, the total capacity decreases where the forward downlink before interference produces 8.99 Gbps to 4.74 Gbps. The return uplink capacity of 7.09 Gbps due to interference becomes 5.27 Gbps. The purpose of further research recommendations is to analyze CCI on other reuse color schemes with a more significant number of beams and analyze appropriate mitigation techniques.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-Based Wetland Vegetation Classification: The Impact of Spectral and Spatial Features
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Asia-Pacific Conference on Geoscience, Electronics and Remote Sensing Technology (AGERS)
abstract: Wetlands are intricate and dynamic ecosystems essential for biodiversity conservation, water purification, and climate regulation. Effective management and conservation planning for wetlands, particularly emergent marsh ecosystems of high conservation priority, require precise vegetation classification. However, traditional classification methods often struggle to address the spatial heterogeneity and complexity of wetlands. In addition, the high costs and time demands of repeated, accurate surveys have hindered efforts to monitor plant species and vegetation cover in semi-permanent emergent marshes. This study integrates deep learning models with high-resolution imagery from the National Agriculture Imagery Program (NAIP), leveraging spatial and spectral features to classify and evaluate wetland vegetation in semi-permanent emergent marshes within the Arkansas Delta. The proposed framework provides a robust and automated approach for detecting and assessing changes in vegetation cover. Results demonstrate that incorporating both spectral and spatial features significantly improves classification accuracy, particularly for vegetation categories with overlapping spectral signatures. The Kappa coefficient ranged from 0.56 to 0.94, while overall accuracy spanned 67.8<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> to 95.5% across various combinations. Statistical analyses further revealed significant interactions between band combinations, rotation effects, and model performance, influencing both accuracy and processing time. These findings offer valuable insights for wetland managers and stakeholders, particularly for estimating habitat quality for species such as the King Rail (Rallus elegans) and assessing energetic resources for wintering waterfowl. By applying deep learning to wetland vegetation classification, this study highlights the transformative potential of scalable and efficient monitoring tools, paving the way for innovative and data-driven conservation strategies.

articleTitle: Implementing Agile Design and Standard Work Hour Model via Dashboard Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Asia-Pacific Conference on Geoscience, Electronics and Remote Sensing Technology (AGERS)
abstract: Agile design and standard work hour models are fundamental to enhancing efficiency in modern manufacturing and service sectors. This study examines the integration of these models through advanced dashboard monitoring systems, emphasizing their impact on operational efficiency and customer satisfaction. By facilitating real-time data collection and analysis, dashboards empower managers to optimize processes and align designs with standardized work schedules. The study reveals that dashboards not only streamline production but also reduce lead times and production costs by balancing flexibility with consistency. They enable predictive maintenance, demand forecasting, and continuous improvement through advanced analytics and machine learning, further enhancing resource allocation and productivity. A detailed survey analysis, employing Chi-Square tests and Factor Analysis, underscores the significant benefits of frequent dashboard use in improving routine work, resource allocation, and compliance with delivery schedules. It also highlights areas for enhancement, particularly in integrating financial and sales management functionalities. In conclusion, the strategic use of dashboard monitoring systems provides a comprehensive approach to harmonizing customization with productivity. This approach fosters a robust balance between technological advancements and human factors, leading to sustained competitive advantage and significant improvements in efficiency and performance.

articleTitle: Object-Based Slum Area Mapping using Multispectral and Textural Information
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Asia-Pacific Conference on Geoscience, Electronics and Remote Sensing Technology (AGERS)
abstract: Slums are often found in big cities due to the increase in urban population. The Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) program launched by the United Nations (UN) includes the issue of slums in the 11th goal. Improving slum conditions is a priority in many countries, including Indonesia. Jakarta Province as the largest metropolitan area in Indonesia also faces this problem. The first step to addressing the problem is to identify slums. One method that can be used for this identification is mapping using remote sensing. This research conducts slum mapping using an object-based approach and Random Forest algorithm, using multispectral information, texture, and Open Buildings V2 Polygons as parameters. Based on the research results, the classification using the object approach with the Simple Non-Iterative Clustering (SNIC) algorithm with a segmentation size of 15 pixels has the best accuracy of 0.892. Based on the modeling result obtained B11, which refers to the near-infrared band, and Normalized difference Built-up Index (NDBI) is the most important multispectral feature in the model. Meanwhile, Sum Average (SA VG) is the most important texture feature in the model and Open Buildings V2 Polygons have the greatest importance in the pixel approach but not so much in the object approach.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Smart Fishpond Monitoring System Using LoRa Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Asia-Pacific Conference on Geoscience, Electronics and Remote Sensing Technology (AGERS)
abstract: Indonesia is a maritime country with large income potential in the fisheries sector, both seawater and freshwater fisheries. This potential is very visible in the number of seawater and freshwater fish catches. This research focuses on monitoring pond water fisheries in the form of water turbidity and location points. The reason is because there are obstacles in pond management starting from the initial preparation of the pond until the fish seeds are introduced, then there is the pond maintenance process including feeding, the process of maintaining water turbidity quality, and the production process. One important aspect in increasing fishpond harvest production is understanding the correlation between several water parameters such as temperature, pH, dissolved oxygen levels and salinity with fish health and growth. So, to obtain optimal results, it is necessary to develop a Long Range (LoRa) based fishpond management monitoring system with the main aim of increasing fishpond harvest production. Early detection of changes in water quality and other factors is useful for preventing potential problems that can affect fish health and crop yields. In this research, we obtained the results of optimizing the LoRa communication system in sending the required sensor data such as location sensor data, water turbidity sensors, RSSI values and SNR values, for the RSSI value range, namely -119 dBm to -64 dBm. And the SNR value ranges from 3.48 dB to 11.02 dB. This demonstrates that the system we developed complies with the LoRa communication standards.

articleTitle: Development of Geographical Information System for Mangrove Monitoring (Case Study: Mangrove Malang Indonesia)
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Asia-Pacific Conference on Geoscience, Electronics and Remote Sensing Technology (AGERS)
abstract: Mangrove monitoring is crucial in Kabupaten Malang, a region known for its 18 beaches. The increasing trend of mangrove deforestation, driven by unchecked tourism activities, underscores the need for an effective monitoring system. There is limited oversight from the government, which exacerbates the issue. This study aims to develop a geographical information system for a mangrove monitoring website that provides valuable insights to stakeholders while promoting awareness about eco-tourism practices. The project adopts the prototyping methodology within the software development life cycle to facilitate effective communication between researchers and expert users from Kabupaten Malang. The website was developed using the Django stack, a robust web development framework. User acceptance testing employed the Blackbox method, with results indicating that the system meets all defined use cases. Specifically, six use cases for administrators and three for guests were successfully validated, demonstrating the website's readiness for implementation as a pilot proj ect in Kabupaten Malang. The evaluation phase highlights opportunities for future enhancements, such as incorporating additional user roles to improve privacy and access control, integrating the platform with government systems for broader adoption, and embedding tutorial pages for user guidance. Additionally, real-time data integration from external resources is suggested to improve monitoring capabilities and encourage eco-tourism. These improvements aim to strengthen mangrove monitoring efforts and boost tourist engagement by emphasizing sustainable tourism practices. This initiative offers a promising step toward balancing ecological preservation and tourism development in Kabupaten Malang.

articleTitle: Plenary: Takeo
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Asia-Pacific Conference on Geoscience, Electronics and Remote Sensing Technology (AGERS)
abstract: The Japanese archipelago is a tectonically active region, with crustal deformation driven by subduction of oceanic plates beneath the continental plate. High strain rates in coastal areas have traditionally been attributed to elastic deformation from plate locking. However, inelastic deformation processes, such as brittle and plastic deformation, play a critical role but remain understudied. This research adopts the inelastic deformation model by Barbot et al. (2017) and applies it to GNSS data to estimate inelastic strain structures in Southwest Japan. Using surface displacement data converted via Delaunay triangulation and Green's function for elastic deformation, an inversion method was developed to estimate subsurface inelastic strain. Validation tests with synthetic data confirmed the effectiveness of maximum principal strain and strain energy as indicators of inelastic deformation. Applying this method to filtered GNSS data from Southwest Japan revealed significant inelastic strain near the Izu Peninsula, attributed to the collision of the Izu Block. The results highlight pronounced inelastic deformation at depths exceeding 30 km, suggesting the presence of larger inelastic blocks. This study demonstrates that incorporating inelastic processes provides new insights into crustal deformation not explained by elastic models. These findings have implications for earthquake mechanisms and underscore the need for further studies to refine the approach and apply it to other tectonic regions.

articleTitle: Tutorial: Java Programming for Earth / Geo Scientists
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Asia-Pacific Conference on Geoscience, Electronics and Remote Sensing Technology (AGERS)
abstract: This course introduces participants to the fundamental concepts of Java programming and their application in geoscience. It covers the basics of Java programming, focusing on writing simple Java programs to analyze geoscience data. Participants will learn how to effectively use control structures, basic input/output operations, and core programming concepts to perform scientific computations. The course will also introduce key Java programming paradigms, including object-oriented, descriptive and functional programming. Testing, now an essential practice, is also highlighted. Additionally, participants will learn about the existence of various libraries for working with geoscience data in Java, expanding their toolkit for handling spatial and environmental datasets. By the end of the course, participants will have a foundation in Java programming with practical applications in geoscience research and analysis.

articleTitle: Artificial Intelligence for Mangrove Mapping and Monitoring Using Remote Sensing Imagery and Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) Algorithm with Python
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Asia-Pacific Conference on Geoscience, Electronics and Remote Sensing Technology (AGERS)
abstract: Mangroves are one of the important blue carbon ecosystems that provide numerous benefits for humans and the surrounding environment. The mapping and monitoring of mangrove forests are important information to know the conditions of the mangrove forests. In recent years, artificial intelligence has gained significant attention in the field of remote sensing due to its effectiveness and accuracy for the classification and regression tasks that use remote sensing data. Remote sensing satellite imagery offers advantages such as large area coverage and temporal information which make it suitable for mangrove mapping and monitoring. Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) is one of the supervised machine learning algorithms based on decision trees which utilizes gradient boosting to iteratively build a stronger model by combining multiple weak decision tree models. This talk will cover the application of the XGBoost algorithm for mangrove mapping and monitoring using Sentinel-2 imagery within a specific study area using Python. Attendees will be exposed to the latest developments in artificial intelligence applications for mangrove studies using remote sensing data and will also learn how to map and monitor mangrove areas using the XGBoost algorithm, including calculations of vegetation and mangrove spectral indices as input features, evaluation assessment, and the analysis of changes in mangrove area.

articleTitle: Sustainable Management of Natural Resources: Focus on Forest Resources Management
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Asia-Pacific Conference on Geoscience, Electronics and Remote Sensing Technology (AGERS)
abstract: Forests are vital ecosystems that provide essential ecological, economic, and social benefits. This presentation explores the sustainable management of forest resources, emphasizing their critical roles in biodiversity conservation, climate regulation, and enhancing community livelihoods. Forests act as carbon sinks, support soil health, and sustain the water cycle, playing a key role in mitigating climate change. Additionally, they contribute to economies through timber, medicinal plants, and ecotourism while preserving environmental integrity. Focusing on Sri Lanka, the presentation examines the spatial distribution of forests and trends in deforestation and degradation. It evaluates forest management strategies such as agroforestry (integrating trees into farming systems), community forestry (local governance), commercial forestry (economic outputs), social forestry (community needs), and conservation forestry (biodiversity protection). These practices are analyzed through the lens of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), highlighting their relevance to afforestation, biodiversity preservation, and sustainable forest use. Practical insights are drawn from case studies of the Sinharaja Forest Reserve, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, and the Knuckles Mountain Range, a critical ecological and water catchment area. These examples illustrate challenges and successes in forest conservation and demonstrate the importance of aligning local actions with global sustainability efforts. The presentation concludes by emphasizing the shared responsibility of governments, communities, and individuals in ensuring forest sustainability. It calls for innovative management practices, policy reforms, and active community participation to address challenges like climate change, biodiversity loss, and resource scarcity, ensuring forests' protection for future generations.

articleTitle: Plenary: Tamer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Asia-Pacific Conference on Geoscience, Electronics and Remote Sensing Technology (AGERS)
abstract: As the world confronts increasingly severe disasters—including floods, earthquakes, and conflicts—the need for rapid, accurate, and comprehensive damage assessment has become critical. Remote sensing, with its capability to provide timely, multi-scale, and multi-source data, has emerged as an indispensable tool in disaster management. This session presents an integrated framework for assessing the impacts of global disasters using advanced remote sensing techniques, with a particular focus on satellite imagery, including both optical and radar data. The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) models with satellite data enables precise mapping and monitoring of affected areas, facilitating timely responses, sustainable strategies, and effective risk mitigation. The proposed framework incorporates data fusion and change detection algorithms to evaluate disaster impacts across local, regional, and global scales. Through case studies of recent global disasters—spanning both natural and human-induced events—the framework's effectiveness in assessing damage severity and supporting rapid response efforts is demonstrated. Each case study highlights the value of integrating diverse datasets to address limitations associated with individual data sources, such as cloud cover in optical imagery or signal noise in radar data. The findings underscore the transformative potential of intelligent remote sensing technologies in building resilient societies and fostering sustainability through informed decision-making. This research advances global efforts in disaster resilience and resource sustainability, addressing the pressing challenges of the contemporary era.

articleTitle: Spatial Mapping of Paddy Fields in South Minahasa Regency, North Sulawesi Using Gis and Remote Sensing Data
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Asia-Pacific Conference on Geoscience, Electronics and Remote Sensing Technology (AGERS)
abstract: Rice (Oryza sativa L.) is a source of staple food for the majority of the Indonesian Population, an important commodity to maintain food security. The area of paddy fields in Tumpaan District, South Minahasa Regency was 310 ha in 2018 (BPS South Minahasa 2018) and was 229 .83 Ha in 2023 (South Minahasa Agricultural Office). The area of paddy fields in Tumpaan District has decreased in the last 5 years. Monitoring changes in land cover in the peri-urban areas of Manado City needs to be carried out to identify environmental changes and their causes for sustainable management of natural resources, especially to ensure food security for the community. This research aims to map the area of paddy rice fields in Tumpaan District during the period of 5 years using Geographic Information System (GIS) and remote sensing technology. Satellite imagery data from 2018 and 2023 are used in this research. Interpretation of satellite images uses on- screen visual analysis with ArcGIS 10.8 software. The research results show that the area of paddy fields in 2018 was 210.1 Ha and the area of paddy fields in 2023 was 137.27 Ha. 3. In a period of 5 years, there was a decrease in the area of paddy fields in Tumpaan District by 72.83 Ha (from 210.1 Ha in 2018 to 137.27 Ha in 2023). The decrease in the area of paddy fields occurred due to changes in land cover from paddy fields to other agricultural land such as horticulture and secondary crops (palawija).

articleTitle: Malaysia's Policy and Innovation Technology in Biodiversity Conservation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Asia-Pacific Conference on Geoscience, Electronics and Remote Sensing Technology (AGERS)
abstract: Malaysia is a megadiverse country with natural ecosystems consist of an immense variety of wild plants and animals. These natural ecosystems also contain a diverse array of flora and fauna communities. Malaysia's rich biodiversity constitutes an extraordinary natural capital that maintains its natural environment and the life-support systems that give us food, water, and numerous economic benefits. The first National Policy on Biological Diversity was formulated in 1998. Current policy, The National Policy on Biological Diversity 2022-2030 (NPBD 2022-2030), is with the adoption of the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework, adopted after the 15<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> Conference of Parties to the Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD COP15), 2022. NPBD, through its 5 goals, 17 targets, and 61 actions, provides the direction and framework for Malaysia to conserve its biodiversity. However, the country's transition to becoming a developed, high-income nation has exerted various pressures on its biodiversity, leaving many species vulnerable, with some even facing threats of extinction. Other pressures that threaten Malaysia's biodiversity include habitat fragmentation, invasive alien species, pollution, poaching, increasing competition for land, and climate change. Advances in technology and digital innovations, such as artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning (ML), drone, Geographic Information Systems (GIS) and remote sensing, are stepping in to revolutionize biodiversity monitoring. These tools are making biodiversity assessments more efficient, scalable, and cost-effective, thus offering a new frontier for conservation efforts. As the biodiversity crisis deepens, the integration of technology innovation into mainstream conservation monitoring will be the key.
